[2] The claimants' allegations are set out in the account included in their Basis of Claim Forms (BOC Forms).1 The facts supporting their refugee protection claim may be summarized as follows. The claimants are cousins. Being talented XXXX (XXXX) XXXX, they played on good teams and were selected to take part in competitions in the United States (US).

[3] After the principal claimant, XXXX XXXX, took part in a tournament in the US in XXXX 2015, he and his cousin, XXXX XXXX, began receiving threats from young people that they would be hurt or killed because they had been given the opportunity to travel.

[4] Following a tragic incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, in which one of their friends was killed, the claimants' parents took steps for them to leave Haiti.

[5] The principal claimant left Haiti for the US on XXXX XXXX, 2016, arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, and signed his BOC Form on May 4, 2017. XXXX XXXX left Haiti for the US on XXXX XXXX, 2016, arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, and signed his BOC Form on May 4, 2017.
DETERMINATION

[6] The panel determines that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" under the IRPA.
ANALYSIS
Identity

[7] The claimants' identities were established to the panel's satisfaction by means of copies of their Haitian passports filed in evidence.2
Credibility

[8] The claimants' testimony was not credible.

[9] The panel identified several contradictions between the principal claimant's testimony and his written account with regard to the agents of persecution. At the beginning of the hearing, the panel asked the claimants whom they feared. The claimants answered that they feared a group of individuals whom they did not know. In his account, the principal claimant refers to four incidents in which he or his cousin, or both of them, were threatened or attacked, in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, during the XXXX of 2015, in XXXX 2016 and on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

[10] When the panel asked the principal claimant who had threatened to hurt and/or kill them after the first incident in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, after his XXXX practice, the principal claimant answered that he had seen the individuals twice, during subsequent assaults.

[11] In his account,3 the principal claimant relates that during the second incident, which occurred in XXXX 2015, not in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, his cousin, claimant XXXX, was injured during a championship game by one of the members of the gang. However, in footnote 4 in his account, the principal claimant contradicts his own statement in paragraph 10, where he writes, [translation] "I had not seen them before this incident".

argument_evidence.context_text: [12] The principal claimant then goes on to write about a third incident, which occurred after a XXXX practice in XXXX 2016, when he was allegedly confronted by the group of young people in question.
However, in his account,5 the principal claimant states the contrary, writing that he was confronted by the same group of young people in question.
When asked to explain whether the group looked familiar, the principal claimant answered that he did not know who they were and, what is more, that he had never seen them before.

subthemes.text:
[14] The principal claimant's answers are contradictory. Although he stated, at the beginning of the hearing, that after the first alleged incident (in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015), he saw the assailants on two subsequent occasions, the principal claimant's testimony regarding their identities was to the opposite effect. Regarding the second alleged incident, the one in XXXX 2015, the principal claimant stated that he had never seen the assailants before. Regarding the alleged incident in XXXX 2016, he answered that he did not know whether it was the same individuals. Finally, in connection with the assault on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he answered that he did not know the assailants and had never seen them before.

[15] In the panel's view, all these contradictions between the principal claimant's account and his testimony undermine his credibility.

[16] The panel is of the opinion that the behaviour of the claimants, XXXX and XXXX, is inconsistent with that of individuals who are allegedly being persecuted and are seeking refuge. Claimant XXXX testified at the hearing that his parents had learned that the group of young people who had gone to the bar/restaurant on XXXX XXXX, 2016, wanted to kill him and XXXX.

[17] When questioned by the panel, the principal claimant, XXXX, testified that after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he had not moved out of the neighbourhood and had remained at his home until he left Haiti on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

[18] Claimant XXXX testified that after his cousin, the principal claimant XXXX, left Haiti in XXXX 2016, he went to live with an aunt in a different neighbourhood and stopped going out in public. Claimant XXXX testimony is consistent with lines 57 and 58 of the claimants' account. However, when the panel asked when he had gone to live with his aunt, claimant XXXX hesitated for a long time before answering that it had been in XXXX or XXXX2016. When asked to specify how long he had stayed there, claimant XXXX answered that it had been until the end of XXXX 2016. The panel asked claimant XXXX where he had lived from XXXX to XXXX2016; he answered that he had lived at his parents' home.

[19] In their account, the claimants state the following at lines 55 to 57:
[translation]
However, even though a complaint was filed, these young people kept trying to torment us. They came to the neighbourhood to ask around about me and my cousin and threatened to hurt and/or kill us.

[20] Despite this threat, the principal claimant testified that he had even continued playing XXXX and going to practices and had played his last game on XXXX XXXX, XXXX days before his departure. For his part, claimant XXXX testified that, after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he had continued going to XXXX practices on Thursdays and Fridays and had played inter-team games, even against other clubs. Claimant XXXX even stated that, after going to live with his aunt, he had continued to play XXXX.

[21] The panel is of the opinion that the claimants' behaviour is inconsistent with the allegations. The main reason for the claimants' alleged persecution is related to the fact that they are skilled XXXX players, which allowed them to go abroad to take part in tournaments. However, in the panel's view, the fact that the claimants continued to attend XXXX practices and even played in games is inconsistent with that allegation. Being out in the open on a XXXX field made it easy for the agents of persecution to track them down. If anything, after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, one would expect that the claimants would have stopped playing XXXX until they left Haiti.

[22] The panel is of the opinion that the claimants' behaviour is inconsistent with that of people seeking refuge, which undermines their credibility.

[23] The panel is of the opinion that the XXXX 2015 incident of which claimant XXXX was allegedly a victim is implausible.

[24] At lines 23 to 26 of the account, it is stated that claimant XXXX suffered a head injury during a championship game in XXXX 2015 after being shoved into a wall by a member of the gang that was harassing them. Claimant XXXX alleges that he had to stop playing and that, after returning home, he went to the hospital.

[25] When the panel asked him to describe the incident, claimant XXXX explained that a spectator who was a member of the gang that meant them harm came and shoved him up against a wall while he had possession of the XXXX. When asked to explain to the panel how a spectator could have jumped onto the field and harassed a player, claimant XXXX explained that spectators were allowed to stand on the sidelines while watching games. The panel then asked claimant XXXX to describe what happened.

[26] According to claimant XXXX, a spectator approached him from his right and shoved him up against a wall, injuring his head. When the panel asked how this could have been possible, the claimant had great difficulty explaining how it had happened. The panel pointed out to the claimant that, in order for him to have been shoved up against a wall, the assailant would have had to push him off the field. In response to this remark, claimant XXXX testified that everything had happened quickly.

[27] When the panel asked how the crowd, the referees, his coach and his teammates had reacted, all claimant XXXX was able to say in response was that neither the assailant nor anyone else had been arrested and that nobody from his club had seen who had assaulted him.

subthemes.text:
[28] In the panel's view, what is implausible about this incident is the fact that no one from claimant XXXX club saw who had assaulted him and that the alleged assailant was not arrested or apprehended. The panel notes that claimant XXXX was playing in a championship game and had possession of the XXXX when he was assaulted. However, if he had possession, it is reasonable to conclude that everyone's attention would have been on him at the time of the incident and that not only claimant XXXX teammates on the field but also those on the sidelines would have been watching what was happening just before he was hit. The same goes for the coach and the referees. In the panel's view, it is therefore implausible that no one from his club saw the assailant. It is even more implausible that no one was able to stop or subdue the assailant, even though claimant XXXX teammates were on the field and there were referees and even players from the opposing team who could have stepped in.

[29] In the panel's opinion, the incident described by claimant XXXX that allegedly took place in XXXX 2015 is implausible and undermines his credibility.
CONCLUSION

[30] Therefore, the panel finds that the credibility issues raised at the hearing undermine the claimants' credibility to the point that the panel finds that they are not credible overall and does not believe any of the allegations they made in support of their refugee protection claim.

[31] The claimants have failed to establish that there is a reasonable chance that they would be persecuted within the meaning of the Convention or that, on a balance of probabilities, they would be subjected to a risk within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, should they return to Haiti.

[32] In light of all the evidence on the record, the panel determines that the claimants, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

[33] Consequently, the refugee protection claims are rejected.

REASONS FOR DECISION

[1] The claimants, XXXX XXXX (principal claimant) and XXXX XXXX, are citizens of Haiti. They are claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).
ALLEGATIONS

[2] The claimants' allegations are set out in the account included in their Basis of Claim Forms (BOC Forms).1 The facts supporting their refugee protection claim may be summarized as follows. The claimants are cousins. Being talented XXXX (XXXX) XXXX, they played on good teams and were selected to take part in competitions in the United States (US).

[3] After the principal claimant, XXXX XXXX, took part in a tournament in the US in XXXX 2015, he and his cousin, XXXX XXXX, began receiving threats from young people that they would be hurt or killed because they had been given the opportunity to travel.
[4] Following a tragic incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, in which one of their friends was killed, the claimants' parents took steps for them to leave Haiti.

[5] The principal claimant left Haiti for the US on XXXX XXXX, 2016, arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, and signed his BOC Form on May 4, 2017. XXXX XXXX left Haiti for the US on XXXX XXXX, 2016, arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, and signed his BOC Form on May 4, 2017.
DETERMINATION

[6] The panel determines that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" under the IRPA.
ANALYSIS
Identity

[7] The claimants' identities were established to the panel's satisfaction by means of copies of their Haitian passports filed in evidence.2
Credibility
[8] The claimants' testimony was not credible.

[9] The panel identified several contradictions between the principal claimant's testimony and his written account with regard to the agents of persecution. At the beginning of the hearing, the panel asked the claimants whom they feared. The claimants answered that they feared a group of individuals whom they did not know. In his account, the principal claimant refers to four incidents in which he or his cousin, or both of them, were threatened or attacked, in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, during the XXXX of 2015, in XXXX 2016 and on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

[10] When the panel asked the principal claimant who had threatened to hurt and/or kill them after the first incident in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, after his XXXX practice, the principal claimant answered that he had seen the individuals twice, during subsequent assaults.

[11] In his account,3 the principal claimant relates that during the second incident, which occurred in XXXX 2015, not in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, his cousin, claimant XXXX, was injured during a championship game by one of the members of the gang. However, in footnote 4 in his account, the principal claimant contradicts his own statement in paragraph 10, where he writes, [translation] "I had not seen them before this incident".

[12] The principal claimant then goes on to write about a third incident, which occurred after a XXXX practice in XXXX 2016, when he was allegedly confronted by the group of young people in question.4 When the panel questioned him regarding the identities of these young people, the principal claimant answered that he did not know them. When the panel asked whether they were the same individuals as before, the principal claimant answered that he did not know. However, in his account,5 the principal claimant states the contrary, writing that he was confronted by the same group of young people in question.

[13] The principal claimant recounted the final incident, on XXXX XXXX, 2016, during which he and his cousin were allegedly attacked.6 When the panel asked him about the identities of the individuals who had supposedly assaulted them, the principal claimant answered that it was a different group of young people whom he did not know. When asked to explain whether the group looked familiar, the principal claimant answered that he did not know who they were and, what is more, that he had never seen them before.

[14] The principal claimant's answers are contradictory. Although he stated, at the beginning of the hearing, that after the first alleged incident (in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015), he saw the assailants on two subsequent occasions, the principal claimant's testimony regarding their identities was to the opposite effect. Regarding the second alleged incident, the one in XXXX 2015, the principal claimant stated that he had never seen the assailants before. Regarding the alleged incident in XXXX 2016, he answered that he did not know whether it was the same individuals. Finally, in connection with the assault on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he answered that he did not know the assailants and had never seen them before.
[15] In the panel's view, all these contradictions between the principal claimant's account and his testimony undermine his credibility.

[16] The panel is of the opinion that the behaviour of the claimants, XXXX and XXXX, is inconsistent with that of individuals who are allegedly being persecuted and are seeking refuge. Claimant XXXX testified at the hearing that his parents had learned that the group of young people who had gone to the bar/restaurant on XXXX XXXX, 2016, wanted to kill him and XXXX.

[17] When questioned by the panel, the principal claimant, XXXX, testified that after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he had not moved out of the neighbourhood and had remained at his home until he left Haiti on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

[18] Claimant XXXX testified that after his cousin, the principal claimant XXXX, left Haiti in XXXX 2016, he went to live with an aunt in a different neighbourhood and stopped going out in public. Claimant XXXX testimony is consistent with lines 57 and 58 of the claimants' account. However, when the panel asked when he had gone to live with his aunt, claimant XXXX hesitated for a long time before answering that it had been in XXXX or XXXX2016. When asked to specify how long he had stayed there, claimant XXXX answered that it had been until the end of XXXX 2016. The panel asked claimant XXXX where he had lived from XXXX to XXXX2016; he answered that he had lived at his parents' home.

[19] In their account, the claimants state the following at lines 55 to 57:
[translation]
However, even though a complaint was filed, these young people kept trying to torment us. They came to the neighbourhood to ask around about me and my cousin and threatened to hurt and/or kill us.

[20] Despite this threat, the principal claimant testified that he had even continued playing XXXX and going to practices and had played his last game on XXXX XXXX, XXXX days before his departure. For his part, claimant XXXX testified that, after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, he had continued going to XXXX practices on Thursdays and Fridays and had played inter-team games, even against other clubs. Claimant XXXX even stated that, after going to live with his aunt, he had continued to play XXXX.

[21] The panel is of the opinion that the claimants' behaviour is inconsistent with the allegations. The main reason for the claimants' alleged persecution is related to the fact that they are skilled XXXX players, which allowed them to go abroad to take part in tournaments. However, in the panel's view, the fact that the claimants continued to attend XXXX practices and even played in games is inconsistent with that allegation. Being out in the open on a XXXX field made it easy for the agents of persecution to track them down. If anything, after the incident on XXXX XXXX, 2016, one would expect that the claimants would have stopped playing XXXX until they left Haiti.
[22] The panel is of the opinion that the claimants' behaviour is inconsistent with that of people seeking refuge, which undermines their credibility.
[23] The panel is of the opinion that the XXXX 2015 incident of which claimant XXXX was allegedly a victim is implausible.

[24] At lines 23 to 26 of the account, it is stated that claimant XXXX suffered a head injury during a championship game in XXXX 2015 after being shoved into a wall by a member of the gang that was harassing them. Claimant XXXX alleges that he had to stop playing and that, after returning home, he went to the hospital.

[25] When the panel asked him to describe the incident, claimant XXXX explained that a spectator who was a member of the gang that meant them harm came and shoved him up against a wall while he had possession of the XXXX. When asked to explain to the panel how a spectator could have jumped onto the field and harassed a player, claimant XXXX explained that spectators were allowed to stand on the sidelines while watching games. The panel then asked claimant XXXX to describe what happened.

[26] According to claimant XXXX, a spectator approached him from his right and shoved him up against a wall, injuring his head. When the panel asked how this could have been possible, the claimant had great difficulty explaining how it had happened. The panel pointed out to the claimant that, in order for him to have been shoved up against a wall, the assailant would have had to push him off the field. In response to this remark, claimant XXXX testified that everything had happened quickly.

[27] When the panel asked how the crowd, the referees, his coach and his teammates had reacted, all claimant XXXX was able to say in response was that neither the assailant nor anyone else had been arrested and that nobody from his club had seen who had assaulted him.

[28] In the panel's view, what is implausible about this incident is the fact that no one from claimant XXXX club saw who had assaulted him and that the alleged assailant was not arrested or apprehended. The panel notes that claimant XXXX was playing in a championship game and had possession of the XXXX when he was assaulted. However, if he had possession, it is reasonable to conclude that everyone's attention would have been on him at the time of the incident and that not only claimant XXXX teammates on the field but also those on the sidelines would have been watching what was happening just before he was hit. The same goes for the coach and the referees. In the panel's view, it is therefore implausible that no one from his club saw the assailant. It is even more implausible that no one was able to stop or subdue the assailant, even though claimant XXXX teammates were on the field and there were referees and even players from the opposing team who could have stepped in.

[29] In the panel's opinion, the incident described by claimant XXXX that allegedly took place in XXXX 2015 is implausible and undermines his credibility.
CONCLUSION

[30] Therefore, the panel finds that the credibility issues raised at the hearing undermine the claimants' credibility to the point that the panel finds that they are not credible overall and does not believe any of the allegations they made in support of their refugee protection claim.

[31] The claimants have failed to establish that there is a reasonable chance that they would be persecuted within the meaning of the Convention or that, on a balance of probabilities, they would be subjected to a risk within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, should they return to Haiti.

[32] In light of all the evidence on the record, the panel determines that the claimants, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

[33] Consequently, the refugee protection claims are rejected.
Sylvain Fournier
